entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Addl. Standing Counsel
 Coram:
 Justice S.K. Sahoo
 Order
Order No. 18.08.2023
01.
This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
None appears on behalf of the petitioner.

This is an application under section 438 Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner in connection with 1.C.C. Case No.23 of 2021 pending in the Court of learned S.D.J.M., Jajpur for alleged commission of offences under sections 420/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
Perused the complaint petition annexed as Annexure-1.

The petitioner earlier approached this Court for anticipatory bail in ABLAPL No.16475 of 2021 and this // 2 // Court vide order dated 25.01.2022 taking into account that the case arises out of a complaint petition in which after taking cognizance of offences, summons have been issued to the petitioner for his appearance and since there is no apprehension of arrest of the petitioner, this Court was not inclined to entertain the anticipatory bail application, however, observed that in the event the petitioner appears before the concerned Court within a period of four weeks and move an application for bail, the same shall be disposed of as expeditiously as possible by the Courts below in accordance with law.

entities.text: Sahoo vs State Of Odisha .... Opp. Party
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This successive anticipatory bail application has been filed by the petitioner and a ground has been taken in paragraph-5 that after registration of 1.C.C., police investigated the matter, examined the witnesses and searching the petitioner to arrest him.

No order passed by the learned S.D.J.M.,
Jajpur under section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. has been annexed nor the first information report and only a copy of the complaint petition has been annexed to the anticipatory bail application.

Therefore,
there is no material before this Court that the complaint petition was referred to any police station under section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. for registration and accordingly, the F.I.R. was registered and the police is investigating // 3 // the case for which there is apprehension of arrest of the petitioner in connection with that case.
Accordingly, I am not inclined to entertain this successive anticipatory bail application, which stands dismissed.
Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
( S.K. Sahoo) Judge RKM Signed by: RABINDRA KUMAR MISHRA
